Mexican President Tells U.S. Ambassador to Butt Out Regarding Narco-Politicians

Ildefonso Ortiz and Brandon Darby
2 Jun 2026 206
3:38

MEXICO CITY — Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum on Monday told the U.S. ambassador to stay out of internal Mexican politics following recent comments from the American envoy regarding politicians with alleged ties to organized crime.

The exchange marked the latest in a series of tensions between Mexico City and Washington as the Trump administration ramps up pressure on Mexico to crack down on drug trafficking organizations operating with apparent impunity in several Mexican states.

"Mexico is a free and sovereign nation. Decisions about who runs for office, who governs, and who represents the Mexican people are made by Mexicans alone," Sheinbaum said during her morning press conference.

The U.S. Ambassador's remarks earlier this week suggested that certain elected officials in Mexico have benefited from organized crime support — a suggestion Sheinbaum forcefully rejected.

The diplomatic spat comes at a particularly sensitive moment, with bilateral relations strained over migration, fentanyl trafficking, and cartel-related violence along the shared border.

Analysts say the public rebuke reflects Sheinbaum's broader strategy of positioning herself as a defender of Mexican sovereignty even as her government cooperates with Washington on certain security matters behind the scenes.
